prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: sideswipe while changing lanes in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1300; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the right lane of a two-lane service road in Baytown, Texas, when Driver 2 moved left into the same lane without signaling and made contact with the driver's side of Driver 1's vehicle. The sideswipe was witnessed by a pedestrian standing near the curb, who told me the vehicles touched as both drivers were moving at a low rate of speed. Driver 2 confirmed the lane change and the contact when I spoke with him at the scene, and photographs taken there show scraping and a dented panel on the left side of Driver 1's vehicle that is consistent with the impact described by all parties. A passenger was seated in the front right seat, and both the responding officers and the witness confirmed that person was inside the vehicle at the time. Driver 1 reported pain in the left wrist and said it was struck against the door frame, though it is not yet clear whether the injury came from this collision. No prior damage to the vehicle was known to anyone at the scene. Driver 1 identified the vehicle as belonging to a policyholder with whom Driver 1 lives, and Driver 1 is covered as a member of that household. Driver 1 was transported for evaluation.
